title: Tips for Grilling Large Lamb Chops on a BBQ Grill Mat
keyword: grilling large lamb chops on a grill mat
meta_description: Master grilling large lamb chops on a BBQ grill mat with our step‑by‑step tips, seasoning tricks, and how to keep them juicy and perfectly seared every time.
html:
Grilling large lamb chops on a grill mat can feel intimidating, but the right technique turns that thick, flavorful cut into a succulent masterpiece. A BBQ Grill Mat provides a non‑stick surface that prevents flare‑ups, keeps the meat from sticking, and lets you achieve a perfect sear without losing juices. Below are the practical steps you need to nail juicy, caramelized lamb every time.

Why Use a Grill Mat for Lamb Chops?

Lamb chops are thick and have a natural fat cap that can cause flare‑ups on a bare grill. A BBQ Grill Mat acts as a barrier, allowing the heat to circulate while protecting the meat from direct flame. This means:

  • Even heat transfer for consistent doneness.
  • Reduced risk of charring the exterior before the interior is cooked.
  • Easy cleanup – the mat catches drippings and can be rinsed or tossed in the dishwasher.

Because the mat is reusable, it’s also a greener choice for frequent grillers.

Preparing the Lamb Chops

Start with high‑quality, bone‑in lamb chops about 1½ to 2 inches thick. Pat them dry with paper towels—moisture on the surface prevents a good crust. Then:

  1. Season early. Rub each chop with olive oil, then coat with a mixture of kosher salt, cracked black pepper, minced garlic, and fresh rosemary. The oil helps the seasoning adhere and promotes browning.
  2. Let them rest. Allow the seasoned chops to sit at room temperature for 20‑30 minutes. This step brings the interior temperature up slightly, reducing the time needed on the grill.
  3. Optional glaze. If you like a sweet‑savory finish, whisk together honey, Dijon mustard, and a splash of lemon juice. Brush it on during the last few minutes of cooking.

These prep steps are the same whether you’re using a grill mat or a bare grill, but the mat makes the final sear more forgiving.

Setting Up the Grill and the Mat

Preheat your gas or charcoal grill to medium‑high (about 400–450°F). While the grill heats, lay a BBQ Grill Mat directly on the grates. The mat will begin to glow slightly—this is normal and indicates it’s ready.

Place the mat so that the longer side runs across the hottest zone of the grill. This allows you to move the chops to a cooler area if they start to brown too quickly.

Grilling the Lamb Chops

When the grill and mat are hot, arrange the lamb chops on the mat with a little space between each piece. Close the lid and let them cook undisturbed for about 4‑5 minutes per side. Because the mat reduces flare‑ups, you can keep the lid closed for a more oven‑like environment, which helps the chops cook evenly.

Use tongs to flip the chops—avoid piercing them with a fork, which releases juices. After flipping, check the internal temperature with an instant‑read thermometer; aim for 135°F for medium‑rare or 145°F for medium. Remember that the meat will continue to rise a few degrees while it rests.

If you’re adding a glaze, brush it on during the final 2 minutes of cooking, then give the chops one quick turn to set the coating.

Resting, Slicing, and Serving

Transfer the chops to a warm plate and tent them loosely with foil for 5‑7 minutes. Resting lets the fibers relax and the juices redistribute, resulting in a tender bite.

To slice, cut against the grain, starting at the bone edge and working toward the tip. Serve the chops with a fresh herb sauce—mint, parsley, or cilantro mixed with lemon zest works beautifully.

Cleaning up is a breeze. Let the BBQ Grill Mat cool, then wash it in warm, soapy water or pop it into the dishwasher. With proper care, the mat will last for many grilling seasons.

Tips for Perfect Results Every Time

  • Don’t overcrowd the mat; good airflow is key for even cooking.
  • Use a meat thermometer; thickness varies, and visual cues can be misleading.
  • Reserve a small bowl of the pan drippings to drizzle over the finished chops for extra flavor.
  • If you prefer a smoky flavor, add a few wood chips to the charcoal or place a smoker box on the gas grill before laying the mat.

FAQ

Can I use a grill mat on a charcoal grill?

Yes. The BBQ Grill Mat works on both gas and charcoal grills. Just make sure the coals are spread evenly and the mat is placed directly on the grates.

Will the grill mat affect the smoky taste of the lamb?

The mat reduces direct flame contact, but the smoke from the fat drippings still flavors the meat. For a stronger smoke profile, add a handful of wood chips to the fire and keep the lid closed.

How do I clean the grill mat after cooking fatty lamb chops?

Allow the mat to cool, then rinse it under warm water and scrub with a non‑abrasive brush. For stubborn residue, soak it in a mixture of hot water and a few drops of dish soap before washing.
